subject: MSA Annex: On-Prem License Guardrails & Evidence Escrow Proposal
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice@stethoshealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Chen <m.chen@stethoshealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: On-site deployment rights / evidence options for MSA annex

Jonas —

Thanks for the demo last week. We are close to finalizing the Order Form but our legal team needs clearer language in the MSA about two items before procurement will sign:

1) License boundary for on-prem (operator access, retention of model artifacts). We need to ensure we do not get a "broader use" right beyond the runtime required for our workload.
2) Escrow-like evidence: we understand Redwood won't agree to full code escrow. Can you provide a short, prescriptive set of evidence deliverables (snapshots, witness procedure, attestation) that would satisfy our internal auditors?

I've attached an annotated MSA and a draft evidence checklist (attached). Can we get an early draft of an annex or amendment that narrows scope and outlines a limited witness/forensics pathway?

Best,
Alice
Alice Monroe
VP Legal, Stethos Health
[Attachment: Stethos_MSA_Annotated.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: evidence-checklist.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice@stethoshealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On-site deployment rights / evidence options for MSA annex

Alice —

Appreciate the level of detail — this is helpful. Two quick points up-front:

- We can tighten the license grant in the MSA Annex so it explicitly limits use to: (a) the customer-hosted runtime and (b) permitted production use for the named application(s). No broader redistribution or reseller rights.
- For escrow-like evidence, we can't offer source-code escrow, but we can offer a controlled snapshot and witnessing workflow: sealed forensic snapshots, time-limited witness windows, and a neutral third-party hash verification.

I'm looping in our legal and delivery leads to draft concrete language and a short exhibit with options (A/B):
A) On-site witness + sealed snapshot — Redwood prepares a read-only forensic snapshot, witness present during extraction, transfer via signed seals.
B) Remote attestation + periodic snapshot — for customers who cannot accommodate on-site visits, we provide signed attestation artifacts plus periodic encrypted snapshots delivered to a certified custodian.

CC'ing Laura (legal), Rishi (security), and Camila (solutions) to produce the annex text and an evidence checklist that matches your attachments. Expect a draft by EOD 11 Jan.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: OrderForm_v4.docx (DOCX)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: RE: On-site deployment rights / evidence options for MSA annex (internal redlines)

Team —

Attached are internal redlines and my suggested Annex language. High-level notes:

- License scope: propose adding a two-sentence sentence that restricts any copy of model weights to the runtime node(s) used for production inference for the Account's product(s). Add explicit prohibition on commercializing the model beyond the customer's internal product.
- Operator access: define "Operator" as Redwood employees performing agreed maintenance tasks, limited to specific IP ranges and MFA-based ephemeral credentials; require customer approval for permanent operator accounts.
- Evidence pathway: provide both options A and B (Jonas), but add a third: C) Escrow-lite: deposit of an encrypted sealed snapshot with a named custodian with release conditioned on documented termination triggers and joint inspection.
- Audit windows: limit witness windows to two business days and require customer to provide local facilities for any on-site witness activity.

I marked specific clauses to insert into Exhibit C (Private Deployment Annex). I kept the wording narrow to avoid creating a de facto license transfer. Also flagged a clause to tie any forensic snapshot retention period to the Order Form term + 90 days.

I'll annotate and attach a redline to send upstream; Camila, can you validate operational feasibility for options A/B/C? Rishi, confirm the hash/attestation tech (TPM vs software signing) we recommend.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MSA_Annex_Draft_redline.docx (DOCX)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice@stethoshealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Chen <m.chen@stethoshealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed Exhibit C (Private Deployment Annex) + evidence options (draft)

Alice / Michael —

Thanks again for the annotated MSA. Attached is a concise draft of Exhibit C plus an evidence checklist aligned to the items you provided. Summary of the options we propose (consolidated):

Option 1 — Witnessed Sealed Snapshot (preferred for high-assurance audits)
- Redwood prepares a read-only snapshot of runtime artifacts required to restore the environment.
- Customer (or their designated auditor) to witness extraction during a two-business-day window; transfer occurs over encrypted media; both parties sign chain-of-custody forms.
- Redwood retains hash and signature; snapshot retention limited to Term + 90 days unless otherwise agreed.

Option 2 — Remote Attestation & Custodian Deliverable (operationally lighter)
- Redwood provides signed attestation packages (execution logs, binary hashes, operator runbook excerpts) and periodic encrypted snapshots delivered to a named custodian.
- Access to snapshot requires joint approval and documented termination trigger.

Option 3 — Escrow-lite (custodian deposit)
- Encrypted sealed snapshot deposited with a neutral custodian under a three-party escrow agreement. Release conditions limited to insolvency, prolonged failure to support, or other contract-specified triggers.

Key legal protections included in Exhibit C:
- Narrow license grant language tied to the named Account application and runtime nodes.
- Explicit prohibition on redistribution, resale, or derivative model training outside the named application.
- Operator access constrained to ephemeral credentials and logged sessions; local IP allow-listing for on-site ops.

Next steps: If this aligns with your auditors' needs, Laura and I can incorporate your minimal edits and return a v1.1 that procurement can route for signature. If you prefer Option 3 as the base line, we can draft the custodian agreement template for review.

Attachments: Exhibit_C_Draft.txt, evidence-checklist.xlsx

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Exhibit_C_Draft.txt (TXT)]
[Attachment: evidence-checklist.xlsx (XLSX)]

Jonas —

Thanks, this is very close. High-level responses from our side:

- License wording: acceptable as written; procurement will need the final clause tying the license to the Order Form IDs.
- Preference: Option 3 (Escrow-lite) looks best for our audit board — please proceed with a custodian template.
- We will provide the custodian's contact and procurement contact next business day.
- Question: can you confirm that the snapshot hashes will be generated using an HSM-backed key and that Redwood will provide the verification logs for a period of 180 days post-transfer? (this came up in our compliance checklist)

If you can confirm the HSM hash/180-day log retention, we can route this internally and expect a PO by end of next week.

Regards,
